discovery: Photonic crystals: the concept and realization of photonic band gap materials
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that a periodic dielectric can forbid light from propagating in a band of frequencies. Yablonovitch framed it as a way to suppress spontaneous emission, and John as a route to strong localization of photons. Yablonovitch then made the first three-dimensional photonic band gap structure. Joannopoulos turned the idea into a predictive science by applying band-structure methods from solid-state physics to Maxwell's equations. His work showed how defects, waveguides and cavities could route and trap light with near-perfect control. Together their work founded modern nanophotonics. It led to photonic crystal fibers, high-Q nanocavities, slow light, engineered light-matter interaction and, later, topological photonics. Photonic crystals carried the concepts of condensed-matter physics into electromagnetism. They remain the conceptual and practical foundation for integrated photonics, lasers, sensors and optical computing.
